title: Geneva Rising Again
premise: Emrys Dunmore, a disgraced intelligence analyst living off-grid in Geneva, is approached by a woman named Sable who claims he once saved her life — a favor he has no memory of performing. The debt she repays drags him into a conspiracy: a buried dossier proving three governments jointly laundered a massacre, now hunted by an assassin called the Cartographer who erases witnesses along with evidence. As Emrys races to authenticate and move the dossier before a dawn extraction flight, he discovers his own erased memory is the final key to its legitimacy. He gets the truth airborne at terrible cost — Sable dies covering his escape, and Emrys chooses exile over redemption, finally belonging somewhere by belonging nowhere.
about_author: Isandro Yarrow is the pen name of a former logistics consultant who spent a decade shuttling between border cities and now writes thrillers about people who live out of go-bags. He lives in three time zones on purpose and answers to no fixed address.

chapters.title: The Packed Bag
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. A quiet morning in Geneva unravels as we see his rituals: the go-bag by the door, the rehearsed cover story, the job he's about to lose. Emotional beat: brittle control masking dread.

chapters.title: A Favor Returned
chapters.summary: Sable appears at his favorite café claiming he saved her in Sarajevo years ago — a memory he doesn't have. She leaves a burner phone and a warning. His POV; beat: uncanny vertigo, first hook of doubt.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: The burner rings: Sable needs one night of his analytical skills to read a redacted file. Emrys agrees against every instinct. Alternating POV with Sable; beat: reluctant complicity turning to fascination.

chapters.title: The Redacted Massacre
chapters.summary: In a safehouse, Emrys recognizes the document's formatting — it came from an agency that fired him. Three governments' fingerprints overlap. His POV; beat: professional pride reigniting into fear.

chapters.title: Cartography of Death
chapters.summary: The assassin's POV chapter: the Cartographer reviews a map of Geneva with two names circled, methodical and almost tender. Beat: cold dread established from inside the hunter's mind.

chapters.title: Old Colleagues, New Questions
chapters.summary: Emrys contacts his former handler Marta for verification and realizes she already knows about the dossier — and wants it buried. His POV; beat: betrayal by the institution that shaped him.

chapters.title: Sarajevo, Remembered Wrong
chapters.summary: Sable's POV: flashbacks of the event Emrys supposedly prevented, but details don't match his own memories. Beat: the mystery turns inward — whose past is fabricated?

chapters.title: The Safehouse Burns
chapters.summary: An attack destroys their safehouse minutes after they leave; Sable's contact dies inside. Emrys's POV; beat: survival guilt, the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Lie
chapters.summary: Emrys reconstructs the conspiracy from fragments: a joint operation, a village erased, records laundered through Geneva banks. His POV; beat: the analyst reborn, exhilarated and terrified.

chapters.title: Marta's Offer
chapters.summary: Marta offers Emrys reinstatement if he hands over the dossier quietly. Sable urges refusal. Dual POV; beat: temptation of belonging versus integrity.

chapters.title: The Cartographer Closes In
chapters.summary: Assassin's POV: interrogating a banker, leaving a precise, surgical trail toward Emrys. Beat: tightening noose, reader knows more than the heroes.

chapters.title: Forged and Fractured
chapters.summary: Emrys discovers his own signature on an old memo authenticating the cover-up — evidence he was there and remembers nothing. His POV; beat: identity collapse, memory as unreliable currency.

chapters.title: Run Through the Old Town
chapters.summary: A chase through Geneva's alleys after a meet goes wrong; Sable takes a graze wound saving him. His POV; beat: debt reversed — now he owes her.

chapters.title: The Extraction Deal
chapters.summary: Sable reveals the dawn flight: a journalist ally will fly the dossier out if they reach the airfield by 5 a.m. Her POV; beat: fragile hope with a hard deadline.

chapters.title: What the Bag Carries
chapters.summary: Quiet interlude: Emrys unpacks his go-bag, item by item, each object a memory of failures. His POV; beat: elegiac reckoning with the man he became.

chapters.title: Marta's Last Card
chapters.summary: Marta reveals Sable may not be who she claims — possibly the Cartographer's partner baiting him. His POV; beat: trust shattered at the worst hour.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Jet d'Eau
chapters.summary: Emrys tests Sable; she admits a partial lie — she wasn't saved by him, but her sister was, and the sister died waiting for help that never came. Her POV; beat: grief replacing deception.

chapters.title: Night of the Long Shadows
chapters.summary: The Cartographer corners them in a freight depot; a brutal fight leaves Marta dead protecting the dossier — her final act of conscience. Dual POV; beat: costly sacrifice, alliances clarified.

chapters.title: Dawn Approach
chapters.summary: Race to the airfield as the Cartographer calls in a government lockdown. Emrys must talk past three checkpoints using only his polished lie. His POV; beat: white-knuckle momentum.

chapters.title: The Flight Leaves at Dawn
chapters.summary: On the tarmac, the Cartographer confronts them; Sable stays behind to hold him off, ordering Emrys onto the plane. His POV watching her fall; beat: devastating climax, the price paid in full.

chapters.title: Truth at Altitude
chapters.summary: Airborne, Emrys watches the dossier transmit worldwide as the journalist publishes. Geneva wakes to headlines. His POV; beat: hollow victory, truth delivered but unbearably bought.

chapters.title: Belonging Nowhere
chapters.summary: Weeks later, in a nameless coastal town, Emrys packs a new go-bag — lighter now, holding only what's true. He visits no one, owes no one, belongs to himself. His POV; beat: bittersweet resolution, survival accepted.
